notes:
1. Dek says "Microsoft's CEO, OpenAI and Anthropic each put monitoring and a way to stop a model at the center of this weekend's news." Only Nadella's post calls for a way to stop a model ("An authorized person should always be able to pause or shut down a model mid-task"). OpenAI's report says "monitoring must also cover the grader's actions", and Anthropic's says it will turn off live internet access for evaluations "until we have confirmed that our security and monitoring measures ... reliably catch behaviors like these"; neither describes a way to stop a model. Also "this weekend": Anthropic's report is dated "Oct 9, 2026" (a Friday), TechCrunch on it is 2026-10-09, and OpenAI's report is "updated: Oct 9, 2026" (incident Oct 6). Fix: "Microsoft's CEO, OpenAI and Anthropic each put the monitoring of AI models at the center of the news in the past few days."
2. Section 2 says "Nadella's two concrete asks are that every meaningful model action must leave tamper-proof human readable evidence, and that an authorized person should always be able to pause or shut down a model mid-task." Source: Nadella lists seven principles (model diversity, observe everything, verifiability, independent controls, independent auditability, containment, incident disclosure), so "two ... asks" implies he made only two. Fix: "Two of Nadella's principles are that every meaningful model action must leave tamper-proof human readable evidence, and that an authorized person should always be able to pause or shut down a model mid-task."
3. Section 1 says "Those of us in finance know this posture from how we handle staff with system access." No source says what finance firms do or that they handle staff this way; Nadella says "we have learned a lot about how to handle powerful actors inside the enterprise ... (establish identity, limit privileges, log activity, create containment boundaries, etc.)", about enterprises in general, not finance and not staff. Fix: "Nadella notes that enterprises have long handled powerful actors inside them with practices such as establishing identity, limiting privileges and logging activity." (or drop the sentence).
4. Section 5 subheading "Small models may steer the big ones" says more than the source. Decoder/Microsoft: it "has 'the potential' to 'guide and control agents through complex environments'"; nothing says it steers larger models. Fix: "A small model pitched to steer agents".
